japan.label: Japan

studies.source: BOJ Outlook Report, Jan 2026, Box 3 (Q-JEM, standard model)
studies.note: Chart B3-6 shows a 5% yen fall: +0.13 / +0.30 / +0.47pt on CPI ex fresh food; scaled linearly x2 to 10% (values read off the chart, +/-0.03).

studies.source: BOJ Outlook Report, Jan 2026, Box 3 (Q-JEM, structural-change model — post-2015 higher pass-through)
studies.note: Same chart: 5% shock = +0.19 / +0.50 / +0.80pt; x2 for 10%. BOJ cautions the post-2015 coefficient comes from a short, mostly-weakening-yen sample.

studies.source: BOJ Outlook Report, Jan 2026, Box 3 (VAR, CPI ex fresh food & energy; 2001-2025 sample)
studies.horizon: yoy peak at 3-4 quarters (2001-21 sample ~0.1 → 2001-25 sample ~0.3)
studies.note: Chart B3-4[1]: 5% depreciation raises the yoy rate by ~0.05 (to 2021) / ~0.15pt (to 2025) at the peak; cumulative level ~0.3pt (2001-25) by 12 quarters; x2 for 10%. Shows pass-through rising in recent years.

studies.source: BOJ Outlook Report, Apr 2026, Box 3 risk scenario (Q-JEM): Dubai crude ~$105 through end-2026, yen -10%, equities -20%
studies.note: CPI ex fresh food 3.1 / 3.0 / 2.3% vs baseline 2.8 / 2.3 / 2.0%; cumulatively +1.2pp. Oil, yen and equity effects are NOT separable in the published figures.

studies.source: BOJ staff working paper (Sasaki, Yamamoto, Nakajima 2023) nonlinear pass-through — as cited by Daiwa, Apr 2026 (secondary citation)
studies.note: ~0.024pt per 1% yen move above the threshold (2000-2023 sample), ~0.0365pt per 1% (Daiwa's 2000-2025 update); below the threshold effect is near zero. x10 for a 10% move already beyond the threshold.

studies.source: Daiwa Securities, Mar 2026 (equilibrium price model, 50% firm pass-through)
studies.note: Crude +50% lifts CPI ~0.6pt; pro-rated linearly to +10% (~0.12pt). Not a BOJ number.

qualitative: BOJ does not publish a per-10% crude-oil rule of thumb for CPI. Apr 2026 Outlook Box 2 gives the transmission: a +100% crude shock lifts petrochemical basic products ~47% within a month, synthetic resins ~18% in 3-5 months, plastics/rubber ~6% within 6 months, and final goods/services (autos +3.8%, accommodation/eating out +3.1%) within ~12 months; first-round pass-through is ~50% (all industries) / ~25% (manufacturing) smaller than in the 1970s oil crises.

BOJ Jul 2026 Outlook: oil pass-through is running faster than in 2022 in business-to-business prices and is expected to spread to a wide range of consumer prices; a Jul Box also finds a global-demand shock lifts CPI ex food & energy persistently (+0.6% after 12 quarters per 1 s.d.).
No official BOJ wage-to-CPI sensitivity was located for this compilation (flagged as a gap).

Rule-of-thumb; sits between BOJ's yr1 (0.26-0.38) and yr2 (0.60-1.0) Q-JEM responses.
Rule-of-thumb; above BOJ's VAR peak yoy (~0.1-0.3) and below the Q-JEM cumulative level.

korea.label: Korea

studies.source: Bank of Korea, 'Price stability target operation review, H1 2026' (17 Jun 2026) — via Seoul Economic Daily
studies.horizon: passes into industrial goods & services with ~6m lag; lasts ~1yr
studies.note: Oil +10% raises core inflation by up to 0.1pt; indirect effects explain ~20% of CPI inflation in an oil-decline phase.

studies.source: KDI, 'Impact of recent international oil price increase on consumer prices' (May 2026) — Dubai crude +10%
studies.note: CPI +0.11pt for an ordinary oil rise vs +0.20pt when the rise comes from shipping/transport uncertainty (Hormuz). Petroleum products +2.0pt vs +2.7pt. Core ~0 vs +0.10pt.
Ordinary oil rises barely move core; transport-uncertainty-driven rises add ~0.10pt.

Oil shock from transport disruption could add 1.0-1.6pt to 2026 CPI; 2026 baseline contribution +1.2pt, 2027 +0.9pt; prolonged-high-oil case +1.6 / +1.8pt. Fuel-tax cuts and the price ceiling took roughly 1pt off by Apr-May (BOK/KDI).

studies.source: Hyundai Research Institute (10 May 2026) — via Edaily
studies.note: 10% won depreciation lifts CPI ~0.3pt within 3 months and ~0.5pt at 6 months via import prices (+8-9% at once); larger in a combined oil+FX shock. Private think-tank, not BOK.

qualitative: BOK Working Paper 2023-11 (Kim & Kwark): global shocks hit PPI/import prices more than CPI/core; energy tracks the global factor, the exchange rate tracks the country factor. BOK Monthly Bulletin 2022-4: global-factor commodity inflation raises inflation expectations more than block-specific rises.

BOK did not publish a won-to-CPI rule of thumb in the sources reviewed; BOK's Dec-2025 inflation report said a sustained ~1,470 KRW/USD could keep 2026 headline inflation in the early-to-mid 2% range (qualitative).

ours.note: Local projections 2008-latest (see Korea site, Inflation tab). 90% band wide; sample pre-dates fuel-tax cuts/price cap.
Brent and the won are correlated; estimated jointly.

taiwan.label: Taiwan

shock_labels.admin: Administered prices — effect of the stated hike (not per 10%)

studies.source: CBC board meeting minutes, 19 Mar 2026 — Brent full-year average assumption $58.3 → $85 (+46%)
studies.note: CBC estimates +0.52pt on 2026 CPI for the +46% oil assumption; pro-rated linearly to +10% (~0.11pt).

studies.source: Same CBC minutes — net of the government's energy-price stabilisation mechanism (-0.35pt)
studies.note: Net effect +0.17pt for the +46% oil assumption (CBC raised its 2026 CPI forecast 1.63% → 1.80%, core 1.75%); pro-rated to +10% ≈ 0.04pt. Shows how much smoothing (CPC pump pricing, fuel-tax measures) dampens pass-through.

studies.source: CBC, Mar 2022 (reported by China Times) — Brent $83 → $110 (+32%)
studies.note: CBC estimated +0.5 to +0.7pt on 2022 CPI; pro-rated to +10% (secondary report of CBC's calculation).

studies.source: CBC Governor Yang Chin-long, post-board press conference 19 Mar 2026 (via TaiSounds)
studies.note: '1% NT dollar depreciation lifts CPI yoy by about 0.05–0.15pt' (full-year average 31.17 → ~31.8, i.e. ~2% depreciation); x10 for 10% (linear scaling is an assumption; the range is wide).

studies.source: CBC Governor Yang, Nov 2022 (via CNA) — NT dollar 6% weaker on average
studies.note: 'Average 6% depreciation adds about 0.15–0.30pt to CPI'; scaled to 10%. Earlier CBC remarks (Jun 2022): NT$29.5 average → +0.12–0.25pt, NT$29 → +0.10–0.17pt.

studies.source: CBC Governor Yang, 20 Mar 2025 (via cnyes) — household electricity +8%
studies.horizon: direct effect on annual CPI (if from April)
studies.note: CBC's own direct-effect estimates in the 2025 forecast: household electricity +8% → +0.09pt (≈0.011pt per 1%); Taiwan Railways fares +26.8% → +0.04pt; water +40% → +0.06pt. Pass-through to firms' prices not estimated.

qualitative: CBC's Sep-2026 forecasts: CPI 2.03% (2026) / 1.83% (2027); core CPI 2.16% / 1.89% (core = ex vegetables, fruit & energy). Jan–Aug 2026 averages: CPI 1.84%, core 2.11%. The Bank raised its 2026 forecasts citing persistently high oil prices and sticky services inflation. Comparison table on this tab.

CBC's framework: Taiwan is a small open economy where ~90% of imports are raw materials and capital goods that feed CPI directly or after processing; NT dollar appreciation lowers NT$-priced import prices and helps contain imported inflation (CBC price-section reviews).

CBC staff Phillips-curve work (search summary only — not independently verified): international oil prices lift inflation over the next 1–3 quarters, with the effect fading after about a year; energy-stabilisation measures shorten and dampen it.
Not found / not compiled: a CBC wage-to-CPI sensitivity; CBC's electricity-tariff assumption for 2027 (DBS says a ~12.8% rise is conditional on the November local elections).

ours.note: Local projections 2008-latest (Korea site, Inflation tab → Taiwan). Pump pricing is smoothed, so noisy.
DGBAS core CPI (ex vegetables, fruit & energy).
